planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun.

directions: Wedgwood Blue bears dense, upright trusses of single, soft lavender-blue florets with the full, classic lilac fragrance. It grows into a naturally compact, rounded shrub that stays more manageable than many older French hybrid lilacs, making it a good fit for smaller gardens. Deadhead spent trusses after bloom and thin out a few of the oldest canes every few years to keep flowering concentrated on vigorous younger wood. Like other common lilac cultivars it needs a real winter chill to set flower buds well.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun, allowing room for a large mature specimen.

directions: Agincourt Beauty is grown for unusually large, single florets in a deep reddish-purple shade, among the darkest-colored flowers found on any common lilac cultivar, carried in substantial, strongly fragrant trusses. The shrub grows upright and vigorous, eventually forming a large, multi-stemmed specimen if left unpruned. Remove a portion of the oldest canes at ground level every few years to keep new flowering wood coming and prevent the base from becoming congested. It needs a cold winter dormancy period to flower reliably and performs best in full sun with good air movement.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun.

directions: Marie Legraye is an old European cultivar valued for its clean, pure white, single flowers packed into dense, well-formed trusses with the strong, sweet fragrance typical of common lilac. It grows as a relatively compact, floriferous shrub, long favored by growers for its reliably heavy bloom even on smaller specimens. Deadhead after flowering and renewal-prune a few of the oldest stems periodically to keep it vigorous. It requires a cold winter rest period to flower well, like other common lilac selections.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun.

directions: Mont Blanc produces large, single, pure white florets held in substantial, well-filled trusses, with the strong, sweet fragrance typical of common lilac. It forms a vigorous, upright shrub and is valued among single white lilac cultivars for the size and purity of its flowers. Thin out old, thick canes at the base every few years to keep bloom concentrated on younger wood, and deadhead spent trusses promptly once flowering finishes. It needs a genuine winter chill to set buds and bloom well.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun, allowing room for a large mature specimen.

directions: President Grevy carries large, fully double florets in a soft blue-lilac shade, held in substantial trusses with the rich, classic lilac fragrance, and is regarded by lilac specialists as one of the finest of the older French double-blue cultivars. It grows into a vigorous, upright, multi-stemmed shrub and tends to produce especially large bloom trusses once established. Deadhead after flowering and remove some of the oldest canes at ground level periodically to maintain vigorous flowering wood. Like other common lilac selections it requires a cold winter dormancy period to flower reliably.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun.

directions: Michel Buchner bears densely packed, fully double florets in a soft rosy-lilac to mauve-pink tone, giving the trusses a fuller, more textured look than single-flowered lilacs, along with strong classic fragrance. It is one of the older French double cultivars still grown for the density and quality of its bloom clusters. Grow in full sun with good air circulation, deadhead spent trusses, and thin out old canes every few years to renew flowering wood. It needs a real winter chill to flower well.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun.

directions: Madame Casimir Perier opens from blush-pink buds into fully double, creamy white florets packed into dense, well-formed trusses, and is considered among lilac specialists to be one of the finest double white common lilac cultivars raised. The strong, classic lilac fragrance carries well, and the shrub grows upright and vigorous once established. Deadhead after bloom and periodically remove the oldest canes at the base to keep flowering concentrated on younger wood. It requires a cold winter rest period, like other common lilac cultivars, to bloom dependably.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun, allowing room for a large mature specimen.

directions: Victor Lemoine, named for the French nurseryman behind so many classic common lilac cultivars, bears large, fully double florets in a rich blue-violet shade held in substantial, well-filled trusses with strong lilac fragrance. It forms a vigorous, upright, multi-stemmed shrub typical of the older French hybrid lilacs. Deadhead spent trusses promptly after bloom and thin out a portion of the oldest wood every few years to keep flowering strong on younger canes. It needs a genuine winter chill period to set flower buds well.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun.

directions: Mount Baker is an early-flowering hyacinthiflora hybrid that opens single, pure white florets up to two weeks before most common lilac cultivars begin to bloom, giving an early burst of fragrant color in the lilac season. Like other hyacinthiflora hybrids it often develops attractive orange-red fall foliage color, a trait uncommon in common lilac. It grows as a vigorous, upright, multi-stemmed shrub and should be pruned immediately after flowering, since next year's buds form soon after bloom finishes. It needs a real winter chill to flower well and performs best in full sun with good air circulation.

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun.

directions: Blue Hyacinth is another early hyacinthiflora hybrid, opening single, pale lavender-blue florets well ahead of common lilac and typically showing good orange-to-burgundy fall foliage color as the growing season ends. The shrub grows upright and vigorous, producing well-filled trusses with the classic sweet lilac fragrance. Prune immediately after flowering to avoid removing next year's flower buds, and thin out old canes periodically to keep the shrub from becoming congested. It requires a cold winter dormancy period to bloom reliably, like other hyacinthiflora selections.
